treatments.title: NeuroStar TMS Therapy for depression

certification.label: NeuroStar University Certified
certification.summary: Central Texas Mental Health is a NeuroStar University certified practice, with specialized training in NeuroStar TMS treatment.

treatments.summary: When antidepressants have not brought enough relief, TMS offers a different way to treat depression. It uses magnetic stimulation rather than medication and does not require surgery or anesthesia.

seo.title: TMS Therapy in Round Rock | Central Texas Mental Health
seo.description: Learn what TMS is, why it is used for depression, and what treatment involves. Central Texas Mental Health in Round Rock.

sections.heading: What is TMS?
paragraphs: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a noninvasive treatment that delivers focused magnetic pulses through a coil placed against the scalp. These pulses stimulate brain circuits involved in mood regulation, with the goal of reducing depression symptoms.
TMS is not an antidepressant medication. You remain awake during treatment, without sedation or anesthesia.

sections.heading: Why is TMS used for depression?
paragraphs: Depression can continue to affect your energy, interest in life, and ability to manage everyday tasks even after trying medication. TMS offers another treatment option when antidepressants have not helped enough or have been difficult to tolerate.

Research supports TMS for reducing depression symptoms. The aim is meaningful relief that helps you return to daily life; the degree and timing of improvement vary. TMS can be part of a broader plan that also includes medication or talk therapy.

sections.heading: What does treatment feel like?
paragraphs: You sit in a chair while the coil delivers magnetic pulses. You may hear clicking and feel tapping on your scalp. Before treatment begins, the clinician identifies the treatment area and adjusts the stimulation settings.

A typical course involves appointments five days a week for four to six weeks. Session length and the full schedule depend on the device and treatment plan. This is a general expectation, not a fixed schedule for every patient.

sections.heading: How is progress assessed?
paragraphs: Your clinician reviews changes in symptoms and daily functioning throughout treatment. Improvement may build over a series of sessions. Follow-up care depends on your response and whether symptoms return.

sections.heading: Safety and suitability
paragraphs: Headache and scalp discomfort can occur; seizures are a rare risk. Tell your clinician about any seizure history, implanted devices, or metal in or near your head. Some implants or metal can make TMS unsuitable.
An evaluation considers your depression, previous treatments, and medical history before deciding whether TMS is appropriate.

treatments.name: Spravato
treatments.title: Spravato for treatment-resistant depression
treatments.summary: Spravato is an FDA-approved esketamine nasal spray for adults with treatment-resistant depression. It offers another treatment option when antidepressants have not provided enough relief.

seo.title: Spravato in Round Rock | Central Texas Mental Health
seo.description: Learn what Spravato is, why it is used for treatment-resistant depression, and what supervised treatment involves. Central Texas Mental Health.

sections.heading: What is Spravato?
paragraphs: Spravato contains esketamine, a medicine related to ketamine. It is given as a nasal spray under medical supervision, rather than taken at home. It acts on NMDA receptors involved in glutamate signaling in the brain; its exact antidepressant mechanism is not fully understood.

sections.heading: Why is it used for depression?
paragraphs: Trying treatment and still feeling depressed can be discouraging. Treatment-resistant depression generally means that at least two antidepressant treatments have not provided enough improvement. Spravato offers a different medication approach for adults in this situation.

For treatment-resistant depression, Spravato can be prescribed on its own or with an oral antidepressant. The goal is relief from symptoms that interfere with daily life. Response varies, so continued treatment depends on how you are doing.

sections.heading: What happens during a visit?
paragraphs: You use the nasal spray under supervision, then stay for monitoring for at least two hours. The care team checks your blood pressure and breathing and determines when you can safely leave.
Arrange a ride home. Do not drive or operate machinery until the next day after a restful sleep.

sections.heading: How often is treatment given?
paragraphs: For treatment-resistant depression, treatment usually starts twice weekly for four weeks. Visits then become less frequent, depending on response. Your clinician assesses benefit after the initial phase and adjusts the ongoing schedule.

sections.heading: Important safety information
paragraphs: Spravato can cause sleepiness, dizziness, nausea, and dissociation—a feeling of disconnection from yourself or your surroundings. Risks also include increased blood pressure, breathing problems, and abuse or misuse. It carries an antidepressant warning about suicidal thoughts and behaviors, especially in younger patients.

Spravato is available only through a restricted safety program called REMS. Review the Medication Guide and your medical history with your clinician. It does not replace emergency care or hospitalization when needed.

faqs.question: Who do you see, and what kind of care do you provide?
faqs.answer: We provide psychiatric care for adults 18 and older, with a focus on medication management. Supportive discussion may be part of your visit. For ongoing psychotherapy or counseling, we recommend working with a separate therapist.

faqs.question: How do I schedule my first appointment?
faqs.answer: Complete the new-patient request, then call (512) 964-6992 and select option 1 to discuss scheduling. Once your appointment is scheduled, the office will provide intake paperwork to complete before your visit.

faqs.question: Do you accept insurance, and when is payment due?
faqs.answer: We accept insurance, including traditional Medicare, and offer self-pay options. Medicare Advantage plans are not accepted. Copays, coinsurance and outstanding balances are due at your visit. Let us know if your coverage changes, and check your benefits with your insurer. Call (512) 964-6992 for plan-specific coverage and self-pay rates.

faqs.question: How do I request a medication refill?
faqs.answer: Ask your pharmacy to send the refill request electronically or by fax at least five business days before your last dose. If you have run out or have two or fewer doses left, call the office for assistance. Some refills, including stimulant prescriptions, may require an appointment.

faqs.question: What if I need to cancel, reschedule or arrive late?
faqs.answer: Please give at least 48 hours’ notice when canceling or rescheduling. Late cancellations and missed appointments carry fees. If you are running late, call as soon as possible; arriving more than five minutes late may mean rescheduling your visit.

faqs.question: Can I have a telemedicine appointment?
faqs.answer: We offer telemedicine appointments. Contact the office to discuss which appointment format is available for your visit.

faqs.question: What should I do if I need help after hours?
faqs.answer: Established patients can call (800) 544-6444 for after-hours assistance from the on-call nurse. For a medical or psychiatric emergency, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.

faqs.question: Can you help with FMLA or disability paperwork?
faqs.answer: FMLA and disability forms may require an additional appointment so your clinician can gather the information needed. There is a separate fee for each form. Contact the office to discuss the paperwork and fees.

privacyPolicy.heading: Your health information and privacy
privacyPolicy.summary: Central Texas Mental Health protects the privacy of your health information. This page summarizes your choices and rights. Read our full Notice of Privacy Practices for details about how information is used and shared, your rights, and our responsibilities.

resources.title: Read the Notice of Privacy Practices (PDF)
Download the Authorization to Disclose Health Information (PDF)
File a privacy complaint with HHS

sections.heading: Access and correct your records
paragraphs: You can request an electronic or paper copy of your health records and ask us to correct information you believe is inaccurate or incomplete. Contact the office to make a request. If a correction request is denied, we will explain why in writing.
You may also request a record of certain disclosures of your health information and a paper copy of our privacy notice.

sections.heading: Choose how we contact you
paragraphs: You can ask us to contact you at a particular phone number or mailing address. We will accommodate reasonable requests for confidential communication. Let the office know which contact details are safe to use.

sections.heading: How your information may be used and shared
paragraphs: We may use and share health information for your treatment, payment for services and practice operations. Other disclosures may be permitted or required by law, including certain public-health, safety and legal purposes. The full notice explains these uses and their limits.

You can ask us to limit certain uses or disclosures. Some requests may be declined. If you pay for a service in full out of pocket, you can ask us not to share information about that service with your health insurer for payment or health care operations, unless disclosure is required by law.

sections.heading: Your choices about sharing
paragraphs: Tell us your preferences about sharing information with family members or others involved in your care. The authorization form lets you identify recipients and the information you want released. You may revoke an authorization by notifying the office in writing; this does not undo disclosures already made in reliance on it.
Written permission is required for marketing uses or the sale of your health information. The full notice describes when information may be shared without your authorization.

sections.heading: Questions or privacy concerns
paragraphs: Contact the office at (512) 964-6992 if you have questions, want to exercise your privacy rights or wish to raise a concern. You may also file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights. We will not retaliate against you for filing a complaint.
